articles.title: Air Canada cancels all flights to U.S. state due to low demand
articles.summary: The national airline initially entered the market with a flight from Toronto in 2001.
articles.body:
While the number of Canadians going to the U.S. for leisure trips saw a small bounceback over several months last summer, cross-border travel is still at a low unseen in decades driven above all by President Donald Trump's aggressive rhetoric and politics toward the northern neighbor.

According to the monthly numbers published by the Canadian government's statistics agency, the number of Canadian trips to the U.S. in September 2026 was down by 29% compared to two years ago in 2024 — a 31% decrease for car border crossings and a 19% drop for flights.

Air Canada to permanently cut flight to South Carolina in 2027

Airlines have, in turn, responded to the weaker demand by cutting routes to smaller cities that once served a market but now do not bring in enough sold seats.

Air Canada was already scheduled to phase out its routes from Minneapolis and Detroit from Montreal and Indianapolis from Toronto by the end of October. The national airline is now reported to not be bringing back its flight to Charleston International Airport (CHS) from Toronto Pearson (YYZ) for 2027.

As a seasonal route that began in March and last year ended at the start of September, the Toronto-Charleston flight was first launched in 2001 and brought back for the summer of 2024 after being retired during the Covid-19 pandemic.

It was, at the time of launch, the first direct flight to Charleston from outside of the United States. Over the years, it has served both business travelers going between the two cities and the growing travel interest in the city from Canada.

As Toronto was Air Canada's only flight into Charleston, the decision not to bring back the seasonal route marks a market exit from the city and the state of South Carolina.

'We have made the decision to discontinue:' Air Canada on axed Charleston-Toronto flight

According to the analysis from aviation website Simple Flying, the 200 departures and 15,200 seats flown from Toronto in 2024 dropped to just 92 departures and 6,992 seats flown following Trump's Canadian tariffs and repeated comments about making Canada a 51st state in 2025.

As such, Air Canada made the business decision to not bring back the route.

Without commenting on the reasons for the abrupt dropoff in travel numbers, an Air Canada representative confirmed the suspension of the seasonal flight. They said that, above all, its flight network is determined by where its customers are shown to be purchasing tickets.

articles.title: Sangue raro: Hemocentro de Ribeirão Preto mobiliza envio para SC | G1
articles.standfirst: Doação envolveu cidades do interior de SP para atender mulher com anemia falciforme em Florianópolis. Material com compatibilidade de 1 em 100 mil seguiu de carro até Campinas antes de embarcar em voo.
articles.summary: Com compatibilidade de 1 em 100 mil, bolsas de sangue raro saíram do interior de SP para atender paciente com anemia falciforme em Florianópolis.
articles.body:
O Hemocentro de Ribeirão Preto (SP) enviou nesta sexta-feira (23) uma bolsa de sangue raríssimo para salvar uma paciente internada em Florianópolis (SC).

A mulher, diagnosticada com anemia falciforme, não encontrava sangue compatível na rede local, o que mobilizou uma operação conjunta de busca e transporte entre os estados de São Paulo e Santa Catarina.

O material coletado em Araçatuba (SP) e em Ribeirão Preto é compatível para uma pessoa a cada 100 mil.

🔍 Anemia falciforme é uma doença genética e hereditária em que os glóbulos vermelhos do sangue alteram seu formato, dificultando a circulação e a oxigenação do organismo.

Bolsas de sangue raríssimo são levadas do interior de São Paulo para ajudar paciente em Santa Catarina. — Foto: Divulgação/Hemocentro de Ribeirão Preto (SP)

'Incidência é de uma a cada 100 mil pessoas'

Para atender à emergência, o Hemocentro de Santa Catarina (Hemosc) recorreu ao Banco de Doadores de Sangue Raro.

As buscas localizaram dois doadores com o perfil adequado no interior paulista: uma doadora em Araçatuba e outro em Ribeirão Preto.

A coleta do sangue ocorreu na quinta-feira (22). A bolsa coletada em Araçatuba permaneceu armazenada até ser reunida com a unidade de Ribeirão Preto.

A partir de então, as duas bolsas foram transportadas de carro até o Aeroporto Internacional de Viracopos, em Campinas (SP), de onde partiram de avião às 18h desta sexta-feira com destino à capital catarinense.

Equipe do Hemocentro de Ribeirão Preto encaminhou bolsas de sangue raríssimo para paciente com anemia falciforme em Florianópolis (SC). — Foto: Divulgação/Hemocentro de Ribeirão Preto (SP).

Gerente do laboratório de imunohematologia do Hemocentro de Ribeirão Preto, Ana Paula Zanelli explicou que a maioria dos procedimentos exige apenas a verificação padrão de compatibilidade, mas casos específicos demandam uma análise mais complexa.

“Para a maioria dos pacientes, fazemos a tipagem ABO e Rh, o que é suficiente para encontrar sangue compatível. Porém, para alguns casos, precisamos fazer uma compatibilidade maior e testar outros grupos sanguíneos", disse.

Segndo ela, todo caso já é considerado raro quando tem uma incidência menor do que um para 1 mil na população.

"No caso dessas duas unidades que mandamos hoje para Santa Catarina, a incidência é de uma a cada 100 mil pessoas testadas para encontrarmos uma bolsa como essa. Neste caso, é bem mais raro”, afirmou Ana Paula.

articles.title: BC passa a exigir autorização prévia para oferecer crédito a clientes com risco de endividamento | G1
articles.standfirst: Nova regra impede ofertas ativas de empréstimos a consumidores com maior risco de endividamento sem consentimento específico e limita essas propostas a renegociações e condições mais vantajosas. Medida entra em vigor em março de 2027.
articles.summary: Nova regra impede ofertas ativas de empréstimos a consumidores com maior risco de endividamento sem consentimento específico e limita essas propostas a renegociações e condições mais vantajosas. Medida entra em vigor em março de 2027.
articles.body:
Banco Central do Brasil (BC). — Foto: Adriano Machado/ Reuters

O Banco Central (BC) aprovou nesta sexta-feira (23) novas regras para proteger consumidores em situação de maior vulnerabilidade financeira contra ofertas de crédito que possam agravar seu endividamento.

A partir de 31 de março de 2027, bancos e outras instituições financeiras precisarão de autorização prévia, específica e inequívoca desses clientes para fazer ofertas ativas de crédito.

Além de exigir consentimento, a norma limita as propostas a operações que possam melhorar as condições financeiras do consumidor, como renegociação de dívidas , portabilidade de crédito — transferência de um empréstimo de uma instituição para outra — ou migração para produtos mais vantajosos.

As instituições não poderão oferecer novos recursos a esses clientes por meio dessas abordagens.

➡️ A medida faz parte de um conjunto de três resoluções aprovadas pelo BC para ampliar a proteção nas relações de crédito e reduzir situações que favoreçam o endividamento excessivo.

Segundo o órgão, as regras buscam assegurar aos consumidores “ mais proteção e informação sobre as ofertas de crédito que recebem ” e reduzir situações que possam favorecer o endividamento excessivo.

Vale dizer que a regulamentação não impede que os próprios clientes pesquisem e contratem produtos financeiros por iniciativa própria.

Segundo o BC, para todos os consumidores, independentemente da situação financeira, as instituições também deverão disponibilizar um mecanismo claro para bloquear propagandas e ofertas ativas de crédito.

Painel vai reunir informações sobre dívidas

Outra medida aprovada pelo BC prevê a criação do Painel de Dívidas Consolidadas , que deverá ser oferecido pelas instituições financeiras a partir de 1º de julho de 2027.

🔎 A ferramenta reunirá informações sobre as operações de crédito dos clientes para facilitar a consulta ao total de dívidas e ao comprometimento da renda com pagamentos.

Antes de uma nova contratação, os bancos também deverão apresentar simulações dos custos do crédito, explicar seu impacto financeiro e emitir alertas em situações de maior risco.

Inicialmente, o painel mostrará apenas as operações contratadas na própria instituição.

Posteriormente, deverá incorporar dados do Sistema de Informações de Crédito (SCR) , mantido pelo BC, e do Open Finance , sistema que permite o compartilhamento de informações financeiras entre instituições mediante autorização do cliente.

Com a ampliação das informações disponíveis, a ferramenta deverá permitir uma visão mais abrangente do endividamento dos consumidores.

BC também muda regras para crédito pelo Pix

O BC também estabeleceu novas exigências para a oferta de crédito durante a iniciação de transações pelo Pix. A partir de 1º de julho de 2027, as instituições precisarão obter o consentimento prévio e específico do usuário para apresentar esse tipo de oferta.

A norma determina ainda um intervalo mínimo de 24 horas entre a habilitação do serviço e a primeira oferta de crédito. Os bancos deverão disponibilizar ferramentas como simuladores e ambientes para consulta das operações contratadas.

A regulamentação também prevê restrições para determinadas modalidades de crédito relacionadas ao Pix e estabelece regras para devoluções associadas a essas operações. O BC ressalta, porém, que o dinheiro continuará sendo recebido de forma instantânea e integral pelo beneficiário da transação.

As três resoluções, publicadas nesta sexta-feira, integram um conjunto de medidas voltadas a ampliar a transparência nas contratações, reforçar a responsabilidade das instituições financeiras e prevenir o superendividamento.

articles.title: Mais da metade dos municípios do Paraná não têm verba prevista para segurança pública no orçamento  | G1
articles.standfirst: Sem essa previsão, cidades ficam impedidas de acessar verbas federais destinadas a investimentos no setor.
articles.summary: Sem essa previsão, cidades ficam impedidas de acessar verbas federais destinadas a investimentos no setor.
articles.body:
Guarda Municipal de Curitiba — Foto: Pedro Ribas/SECOM

Dos 399 municípios do Paraná, ao menos 247 não previram verba específica para segurança pública no orçamento de 2026. Outros 123 planejaram recursos para a área, segundo um relatório do Tribunal de Contas do Paraná (TCE-PR). Segundo o órgão, 29 municípios não apresentaram detalhes sobre o tema.

➡️🚨 No Brasil, a segurança pública não é uma atribuição exclusiva dos governos estaduais e do governo federal. As prefeituras também podem investir no setor e, inclusive, receber recursos da União para financiar ações na área.

Porém, as cidades ficam impedidas de acessar verbas federais destinadas a investimentos no setor se não há essa previsão de recursos na Lei Orçamentária Anual (LOA).

"Existem alternativas que dependem da articulação e da capacidade técnica dos municípios para acessar recursos que estão no Fundo Nacional de Segurança Pública. Elas dependem da elaboração de projetos, de ter governança...", explica Rafael Ayres, coordenador-geral de Fiscalização do TCE.

Papel dos municípios para a segurança pública

No Paraná, 40 cidades têm Guarda Municipal. A maioria está em cidades com mais de 100 mil habitantes, como Curitiba e Londrina. Porém, cidades menores também podem investir em um sistema próprio de segurança.

Campo Magro, na Região Metropolitana de Curitiba, tem 31.888 habitantes. O município passou a contar com a vigilância de Guardas Municipais há cerca de um ano. São 12 agentes que passam a maior parte do tempo cuidando do patrimônio público e que participam de ações integradas com a polícia.

Além da contratação de agentes, há outras formas de investir na segurança pública. No Paraná, 136 cidades usam câmeras de monitoramento em espaços públicos, por exemplo. Apesar disso, quase a metade dessas câmeras ainda não está integrada. Dessa forma, as informações captadas não chegam à Secretaria de Segurança Pública do estado.

A integração é um dos principais desafios para as administrações públicas nesse tema, segundo o Tribunal de Contas.

"O que o relatório trata como um desafio a ser vencido é questão de interoperabilidade entre os sistemas de segurança, para que o município e o estado não trabalhem como ilhas, para que informação seja compartilhada e o enfrentamento de determinada situação seja mais eficaz", detalha Ayres.

Câmera de segurança em Londrina — Foto: RPC

articles.title: Trump retira tarifa de 50% sobre alguns produtos do Canadá, incluindo madeira e alimentos | G1
articles.standfirst: Medida abrange itens como madeira compensada, papel, máquinas e equipamentos de refrigeração e foi anunciada após pressão de senadora republicana; tarifas haviam sido impostas em agosto.
articles.summary: Medida abrange itens como madeira compensada, papel, máquinas e equipamentos de refrigeração e foi anunciada após pressão de senadora republicana.
articles.body:
O presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, assinou nesta sexta-feira (23) uma ordem para retirar a tarifa de 50% sobre alguns produtos agrícolas e florestais importados do Canadá.

A medida pode beneficiar empresas americanas do setor agrícola que dependem desses produtos.

Entre os produtos que deixarão de pagar a tarifa estão chapas de madeira compensada, alguns tipos de papel, determinadas máquinas, equipamentos de refrigeração e caixas e embalagens para transporte de mercadorias, informou a Casa Branca.

"Esses produtores são uma parte vital da economia do nosso estado e sustentam nossas comunidades rurais e costeiras", disse a senadora Susan Collins, do Maine.

Segundo ela, muitos agricultores e produtores dependem de equipamentos especializados, materiais para embalagens e outros produtos canadenses que não estão disponíveis com fornecedores americanos ou cuja substituição teria custos elevados.

A decisão foi tomada após a senadora republicana pedir à Casa Branca que revisasse as tarifas sobre produtos que afetam empresas e agricultores de seu estado. Ela enfrenta uma disputa acirrada pela reeleição.

Candidatos republicanos de estados do norte dos Estados Unidos que fazem fronteira com o Canadá, como Maine e Michigan, tentam equilibrar o apoio à base fiel de Trump com a busca por votos de eleitores independentes. Esses estados são particularmente afetados pelas tarifas.

Collins afirmou que a medida vai beneficiar produtores de mirtilo, batata, maçã e algas marinhas do Maine.

Collins e seu adversário, o democrata Troy Jackson, discutiram as tarifas durante um debate em 6 de outubro.

Entenda a guerra tarifária entre EUA e Canadá

Em agosto, Trump impôs tarifas de 50% sobre US$ 20 bilhões em importações canadenses . As cobranças entraram em vigor depois que as negociações entre os dois países fracassaram naquele mês.

Desde então, os governos mantêm um impasse comercial. Na sexta-feira, Trump afirmou, porém, que o Canadá está trabalhando para fechar um acordo com os Estados Unidos.

A Casa Branca também informou que determinados tipos de válvulas, carpetes, resíduos e outros produtos serão incluídos na lista de itens contemplados pela medida.

As economias do Maine e de Michigan têm relações estreitas com a do Canadá, que fornecem desde peças automotivas até madeira e equipamentos para a colheita de frutas. Por isso, as tarifas têm impacto significativo nesses estados.

A disputa comercial também tem consequências políticas: os republicanos provavelmente precisarão vencer no Maine e em Michigan nas eleições de 3 de novembro para manter o controle do Senado americano.

Presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, durante comício na Flórida — Foto: Umit Bektas/Reuters

articles.title: Frango pode ficar mais barato, principalmente no Sul, após caso de Newcastle em SC, diz Itaú | G1
articles.standfirst: China, Arábia Saudita, Chile e México suspenderam as compras de frango de Santa Catarina após a confirmação do foco da doença, o que pode aumentar a oferta no mercado brasileiro e reduzir os preços no atacado.
articles.summary: China, Arábia Saudita, Chile e México suspenderam as compras de frango de Santa Catarina após a confirmação do foco da doença, o que pode aumentar a oferta no mercado brasileiro e reduzir os preços no atacado.
articles.body:
Frango pode ficar mais barato, principalmente no Sul, após caso de Newcastle em SC, diz Itaú — Foto: Claudio Schwarz/Unplash

O frango pode ficar mais barato nos próximos meses, principalmente na Região Sul do Brasil, após a confirmação de um foco da doença de Newcastle em Nova Itaberaba, em Santa Catarina , avalia o banco Itaú BBA, em relatório divulgado nesta sexta-feira (23).

O efeito deve ser mais perceptível no atacado e pode se intensificar no primeiro trimestre de 2027, quando a procura dos consumidores costuma diminuir, diz o banco.

Na prévia da inflação de outubro , também divulgada nesta sexta-feira, o frango em pedaços ficou 0,71% mais caro no mês. Em 12 meses, porém, o preço acumula queda de 4%, segundo o Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE).

🔍A DNC é uma doença viral que afeta aves domésticas e silvestres . Em quadros graves, pode causar problemas respiratórios e neurológicos em aves. Em humanos, a infecção é rara e geralmente leve, podendo provocar conjuntivite temporária após contato direto com aves infectadas ou suas secreções; não há transmissão da doença pelo consumo de frango.

A possibilidade de queda nos preços está ligada à suspensão das exportações de frango de Santa Catarina. China, Arábia Saudita, Chile e México , que estão entre os compradores do produto catarinense, anunciaram nesta semana que vão deixar de importar a carne produzida no estado.

Santa Catarina está particularmente exposta porque exporta cerca de 63% do frango que produz , a maior proporção entre os estados brasileiros. Na média nacional, 37% da produção é destinada ao exterior.

Com menos destinos disponíveis, frigoríficos catarinenses podem ter de vender no país parte da produção que seria enviada ao exterior. Isso tende a aumentar a oferta, principalmente na Região Sul, e pode levar as empresas a reduzir os preços para conseguir vender o excedente.

Segundo o Itaú BBA, os frigoríficos também podem enfrentar acúmulo de estoques, aumento dos gastos com armazenagem e logística e maior pressão sobre o caixa.

Por que os preços podem cair após a virada do ano

A possível entrada de mais frango no mercado interno ocorre em um momento em que a produção já está crescendo.

De janeiro a setembro, foram abatidas 3,7% mais aves do que no mesmo período de 2025. Já a quantidade de carne produzida cresceu ainda mais, 6,2%, segundo estimativas do Itaú BBA. Para o ano inteiro, o banco espera que a produção avance cerca de 6%.

Até agora, esse aumento da produção não derrubou os preços porque as exportações continuaram fortes e ajudaram a retirar parte do frango do mercado brasileiro. Além disso, como a ave segue mais barata que a carne bovina, muitos consumidores optam pelo frango, o que mantém a procura aquecida e dá sustentação aos preços.

Esse equilíbrio, porém, pode mudar na virada do ano. Com as restrições às exportações, parte do frango que seria vendida a outros países pode ficar no Brasil, aumentando ainda mais a quantidade disponível.

Ao mesmo tempo, o consumo costuma diminuir depois das festas, quando acaba o dinheiro extra do 13º salário e despesas como impostos, matrícula e material escolar passam a pesar no orçamento das famílias.

Com mais frango disponível e menos pessoas comprando, os preços podem cair, principalmente no atacado da Região Sul. Isso não significa, porém, que o produto necessariamente ficará mais barato nos supermercados, pondera o Itaú.

Isso porque, mesmo que os frigoríficos reduzam o valor cobrado do atacado, o varejo pode não repassar integralmente esse desconto ao consumidor. O preço nos supermercados também inclui custos de transporte, armazenamento e comercialização.

O Itaú ressalta ainda que o impacto sobre os preços dependerá, principalmente, de quanto tempo os países levarão para voltar a comprar o frango catarinense.

Em 2024, por exemplo, após um foco da doença de Newcastle no Rio Grande do Sul, a redução das exportações ficou concentrada em apenas um mês e os preços não caíram. Já em 2025, as restrições adotadas depois de um caso de gripe aviária foram mais amplas e duraram cerca de quatro meses, período em que os preços desaceleraram.

Para o Itaú BBA, o episódio atual deve ficar entre os dois casos, com impacto concentrado em Santa Catarina e no atacado da Região Sul.

articles.title: Volvo Cars shares plunge on losses, job cuts
articles.summary: Shares in Swedish carmaker Volvo Cars plunged Friday after it said US tariffs and strong competition from local brands in China pushed it into a third-quarte...
articles.body:
Shares in Swedish carmaker Volvo Cars plunged Friday after it said US tariffs and strong competition from local brands in China pushed it into a third-quarter loss.

The company also said it would cut about 2,500 jobs worldwide.

Volvo Cars, controlled by Chinese group Geely, reported revenue of 66.9 billion kronor ($6.7 billion) for the third quarter, down nearly 23 percent from the same period last year.

It swung to a net loss of 5.7 billion kronor for the quarter from a net profit of 4.5 billion kronor a year earlier.

Around 1000 GMT, Volvo Cars shares were down over 25 percent on the Stockholm stock exchange.

"We continue to operate in a very tough environment with strong external challenges: de-globalisation, hypercompetition and climate change," chief executive Hakan Samuelsson said in a statement.

In response, the company announced a new five-billion-kronor savings plan it said would lead to about 2,000 job cuts in Sweden and 500 more globally, "through natural attrition and by targeted exit packages to employees".

The company currently employs some 39,300 people worldwide, including 19,500 in Sweden, it said in an email to AFP.

The company, which had bet heavily on electric vehicles, said the removal of consumer incentives for EVs in the United States under President Donald Trump had also hit its margins.

In 2024, Volvo Cars dropped a plan to transition to exclusively EV sales by the end of the decade.

"We are convinced that we have the right long-term strategy addressing these challenges," Samuelsson said.

"However, in the short term, with severely challenged volumes, we need to reinforce our turnaround plan with additional decisive actions, lowering our break-even point and improving cash flows to make us more resilient."

Struggling along with other European auto companies in the face of a difficult global landscape, Volvo Cars last year announced an 18-billion-kronor cost-cutting plan.

In May 2025, the group said it would cut 3,000 jobs and two years earlier, 1,300 positions in Sweden were eliminated.

Calling the third quarter "very disappointing", Samuelsson said the company was struggling in particular in the US and Chinese markets.

In China, the market for "legacy premium brands is in severe decline due to intense competition from new Chinese alternatives, basically eliminating profitability for legacy premium brands," the chief executive said.

The situation led to a nearly 50 percent drop in revenue in China compared to a year earlier.

articles.title: Apple is taking Wall Street's top spot back from Nvidia — for the fifth time
articles.summary: Apple briefly topped Nvidia in market value Friday, a move it has made before that has rarely stuck.
articles.body:
Apple ( AAPL ) is taking Wall Street's crown back from Nvidia — for the fifth time.

Apple briefly topped Nvidia in market value on Friday. It's a move Apple has made before, and it has rarely stuck.

Apple and Nvidia ( NVDA ) are each worth about $5.1 trillion, and the gap between them was less than 1% at Thursday's close. The flip came alongside a record run for Apple's stock and the day the tech giant's $1,999 iPhone Duo hit stores , capping a battle investors had been watching all morning. Nvidia has since moved back into the lead.

For most of the past decade, this wasn't much of a contest. Apple closed as the most valuable US-listed company in about 7 of every 10 sessions since October 2015. Microsoft ( MSFT ) took the top spot in stretches, Amazon ( AMZN ) held it for 12 sessions in early 2019, and Alphabet ( GOOG , GOOGL ) got exactly one day in 2016.

Then the AI boom rewrote the leaderboard.

Nvidia first closed at No. 1 on June 18, 2024. It has held the spot almost without a break since June 2025, interrupted only by a four-session Apple run in late July.

Apple has reclaimed the crown from Nvidia four times before today. Only once did it last, when the DeepSeek scare sank chip stocks in January 2025 and Apple held on into the spring.

Since the start of 2024, the No. 1 spot has changed hands two dozen times, according to Yahoo Finance calculations.

This time, the two stocks are heading in opposite directions. Apple closed Thursday at a record. Nvidia sits about 11% below its Oct. 6 record close after this month's chip rout .

Since that Oct. 6 close, which was also the S&P 500's ( ^IXIC ) record, Apple is the only megacap stock in the green. It's up 4%.

Watch whether Apple can finish the day on top. It hasn't since July 30.

The next big test comes on Wednesday, when Microsoft and Alphabet report earnings. They rank third and fourth, each worth about $3.9 trillion.

articles.title: US consumer sentiment near record low ahead of midterm elections
articles.summary: By Dan Burns Oct 23 (Reuters) - US consumer sentiment edged down to near a record low in October as rising prices because of the Middle East conflict soured...
articles.body:
Oct 23 (Reuters) - US consumer sentiment edged down to near a record low in October as rising prices because of the Middle East conflict soured households' views of the economy on the doorstep of midterm congressional elections centering on affordability issues, a survey showed ‌on Friday.

The University of Michigan's Surveys of Consumers said its Consumer Sentiment Index dropped to 48.0 this month from a final reading of 48.1 in ‌September. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast the index at 46.3, which had also been the index's preliminary reading for October.

October's reading marked the second-lowest on record after the all-time low of 44.8 set ​in May, not long after the Iran war began.

"Purchasing power continues to dominate consumer views of the economy," said Joanne Hsu, the director of the Surveys of Consumers. "Sentiment is now 10% below a year ago and 15% less than February, just prior to the Iran conflict."

The survey results dovetail with political polling data showing voters have a dim view of the economy and President Donald Trump's and the Republican Party's stewardship over it.

Millions of US voters have already cast early ballots in the fast-approaching November 3 midterm election ‌that will determine control of Congress over the final ⁠two years of Trump's term. Polls show Republicans are likely to lose control of the House of Representatives and possibly the Senate as Trump's approval rating in a Reuters/Ipsos poll sits at a record low thanks to the skyrocketing fuel prices unleashed by his ⁠decision to attack Iran in late February.

University of Michigan data broken down by political party affiliation showed the weaker sentiment was led by survey respondents self-identified as independents, who comprise a critical bloc of swing voters. Their sentiment score dropped to 42.4 — just above May's record-low 40.6 — from 47.7 in September, while scores for Democrats and Republicans improved.

The survey showed a ​significant ​upswing this year among independents — and also notably Republicans — citing high prices as a drag on ​their personal finances. Since January, the number of independents referencing ‌inflation pressures as hurting their financial situation rose by 27%, while it has shot up by 52% among Republicans. Similar citations among Democrats, meanwhile, are up by 15%.

Households with no or limited exposure to the stock market — until recently climbing rapidly on enthusiasm for the artificial intelligence investment boom — also have cited high prices as a drag on their finances more frequently than at the start of the year.

articles.title: Your forgotten retirement account could be costing you money
articles.summary: Forgotten IRAs could be quietly draining your retirement savings. Here are a few tips to find your lost accounts, plus expert advice on making a plan for you...
articles.body:

Starting a new job can be an exciting time, and for many people, it's easy to forget about the employer-sponsored retirement account they left behind.

Capitalize, a company that helps people roll over retirement accounts, estimates that 31.9 million 401(k) accounts were left behind or forgotten as of July 2025. Those accounts hold about $2.1 trillion in assets, up almost 30% from mid-2023. The firm says the number of forgotten 401(k)s has almost doubled over the last decade.

Even if people haven't really forgotten about these accounts, doing nothing can still cost them. When 401(k)s are left alone, and the balance is small, that money is sometimes automatically rolled over into an IRA. That can come with several drawbacks, such as hidden fees and limited investment options that may not align with your overall retirement plan.

"The biggest mistake is just never deciding," said David Talley, CFP® at Talley Wealth. "People change jobs, the old 401(k) sits there, and nobody's thinking about what those dollars are for anymore."

What happens to your 401(k) balance when you leave a job?

When you leave an employer, you have a few different options to choose from regarding your retirement account.

Employees with a smaller balance of under $1,000 may automatically be sent a check. Those with a larger balance can still opt to cash out, though this is typically not recommended, as it may incur taxes and penalties for those under age 59½.

Workers can also roll over their 401(k) or 403(b) into an individual retirement account (IRA) at a brokerage.

Alternatively, many workers choose to roll over their 401(k) or 403(b) into their new employer's plan to keep their retirement savings all under one roof. Some employees choose to leave their money where it is, and as long as your balance is over $7,000, most plans allow you to keep your money invested.

Employees with balances of more than $1,000 and up to $7,000 may have those funds automatically rolled over by their plan administrator into a "safe harbor" IRA without that former employee's consent.

This is where choosing the path of least resistance can lead to losing money over time.

How neglecting an old 401(k) can affect your retirement savings

According to a white paper from PensionBee, a retirement provider that offers IRAs, using data from the Employee Benefit Research Institute (EBRI), the number of automatic rollovers is projected to double from 1.1 million per year in 2022 to 2.2 million annually in 2030. By then, an estimated 13 million accounts holding roughly $43 billion in retirement savings could be sitting in safe harbor IRAs, the paper estimates.

The concern with allowing those funds to be automatically rolled over without understanding the terms and conditions of the automatic IRA is that workers could be hindering their own retirement savings progress.

Unlike traditional IRAs, which allow you to invest your funds in practically any stocks, bonds, or funds you choose, safe harbor IRAs are typically ultra-low-risk money market funds that have minimal returns and may come with a number of fees that eat into your balance. The white paper suggests that the longer an account stays in an automatic rollover IRA, the more likely it is to decline in value after one year. After eight years, 4 in 10 accounts were worth less than when they arrived, according to the white paper.

Talley says another common mistake people make with their old 401(k) accounts is cashing out because the balance feels small, and paying tax, and usually a penalty, on money that was supposed to be for retirement.

"The third is rolling everything to an IRA on autopilot without looking at what the old plan or the new one actually does well," Talley said.

If you suspect you have forgotten retirement savings floating around, contact the human resources department at your old employer(s) for the plan administrator information.

Once you track down your money, you can leave it where it is, cash it out if it makes sense for your financial plan, roll it over into an IRA, or roll it over into your current employer's plan.

"Find out what it's invested in and what it's costing you, and then make a decision about it, even if the decision is to leave it alone," Talley said.

articles.title: Saudi Arabia wants to send 10 million barrels of oil a day around Hormuz. A former Treasury official says it may barely move prices
articles.summary: Aramco CEO Amin Nasser says the East-West pipeline will grow by 3 million barrels a day, but the expansion will take two to three years, and the line has bee...
articles.body:
Saudi oil giant Aramco , officially the Saudi Arabian Oil Company, is racing to build a bigger back door around the Strait of Hormuz.

Aramco CEO Amin Nasser said this week that the company is working to raise the capacity of its East-West Crude Oil Pipeline, also known as the Petroline, to 10 million barrels a day from about 7 million today, while running engineering studies on additional export routes. Nasser made the comments to Al Arabiya Business in his first interview since the war began . The plan echoes an announcement earlier this month from Saudi Energy Minister Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman, who told the WPC Energy Congress in Riyadh that the expansion would take two to three years .

The goal is to reduce the kingdom's reliance on the Strait of Hormuz, which has been largely choked off since the U.S. and Israel launched a joint military attack on Iran on Feb. 28. Saudi crude production fell below 7 million barrels a day for much of the war's first six months, down from more than 10 million before the conflict, and recovered to about 8 million in September, according to the International Energy Agency .

The Petroline spans Saudi Arabia, running roughly 750 miles from the Abqaiq processing hub near the Persian Gulf to the port of Yanbu on the Red Sea . Before the war, it typically carried around 2 million barrels a day. Aramco ramped it up within weeks, and the line hit its full 7 million-barrel capacity by late March, with about 2 million of those barrels feeding Saudi refineries rather than export markets. The pipeline helped Aramco post a 25% jump in first-quarter profit . Adding another 3 million barrels a day would be a major undertaking.

But it may have little tangible impact on world fuel prices, according to Gilbert Metcalf , a visiting professor at the MIT Sloan School of Management and a former deputy assistant secretary for environment and energy at the U.S. Treasury Department.

"If—and this is a big if—the Saudis can increase pipeline flow to 10 million barrels per day, it will put about 2% more oil into the global marketplace," Metcalf tells Fortune . "That could lower prices a bit, but there's a lot of uncertainty here. The pipeline is vulnerable to drone and missile attacks, as is much of the Saudi petroleum infrastructure. And it's not entirely clear that there is available refinery capacity to process the oil."

That vulnerability isn't hypothetical. The Petroline was first hit in May 2019, when Houthi drones struck a pumping station . This year it has been attacked repeatedly. An April 9 strike on a pumping station cut throughput by about 700,000 barrels a day before Saudi Arabia restored full capacity days later. On Sept. 10, drones struck the line in the Riyadh and Medina regions; Saudi officials said they were launched from Iraq . The attack forced a precautionary shutdown that lasted until Sept. 22, according to Kpler . And a Saudi energy-sector source told AFP that an Oct. 4 attack on a pumping station in Khurais halted flows again , though Bloomberg reported that oil continued to move.

Memory and data storage stocks are shaking off some of their blues.

articles.title: The AI sell-off is crushing stocks of companies leading the data center build-out
articles.summary: Bloom Energy and Comfort Systems just posted blowout quarters, and Wall Street is dumping their stocks anyway as the AI data center trade cracks.
articles.body:
Two of the AI building boom's biggest suppliers just posted blowout quarters. Wall Street is dumping them anyway.

Bloom Energy ( BE ), whose fuel cells generate power on-site at data centers, said Thursday that sales jumped 138% last quarter and raised its full-year outlook to roughly 122% growth. Comfort Systems ( FIX ), which installs the cooling and electrical systems inside them, said its backlog nearly doubled to $17.8 billion.

Both stocks are falling hard for a second straight day. Credo ( CRDO ), which makes networking parts for data centers, is sliding with them.

"A company can deliver extraordinary numbers, but if investors aren't willing to reward those results, something isn't right," Steve Strazza of All Star Charts wrote Friday morning .

Bloom did give the bears something to chew on. Its cash flow turned negative in the quarter, and its margins aren't keeping pace with sales.

Since the S&P 500's ( ^IXIC ) Oct. 6 record close, the companies building and equipping AI data centers are down a median 23%, according to Yahoo Finance calculations. That group includes heavyweights like Caterpillar ( CAT ), GE Vernova ( GEV ), Vertiv ( VRT ), and Eaton ( ETN ).

Power producers are down 14%. Nvidia ( NVDA ) is off 11%. The Big Tech companies writing the checks are down just 5%.

In other words, the companies cashing the checks are falling harder than the ones writing them.

That's backward for a build-out whose biggest problem is supply. "The biggest constraint right now for the AI build-out is power," Jefferies' Aniket Shah told Yahoo Finance on Wednesday, pointing to public pushback against new data centers . Even Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said builders have to be good neighbors .

Apollo chief economist Torsten Sløk wrote this week that demand for computing power is "significantly greater than supply." That means a slower build-out should actually help owners of scarce capacity, he argued, from power producers to transformer makers, where lead times run "up to 26 months." The losers would be "developers and construction-stage investors" and AI stocks priced for everything to arrive on time. (Disclosure: Yahoo is a portfolio company of funds managed by affiliates of Apollo Global Management.)

The real risk, Sløk wrote, is that "scarcity unwinds" if supply catches up or demand softens. Now even his would-be winners are falling. That's the market betting on the worst case.

Together, a dozen of the biggest builders and power names have shed more than $300 billion in market value since Oct. 6.

articles.title: Trump's housing affordability order targets costs that hundreds of thousands of homeowners pay each year
articles.summary: President Trump's new housing affordability executive order targets areas including mortgage insurance, title insurance and manufactured housing construction...
articles.body:
President Trump signed an executive order designed to address housing affordability. Among his targets is mortgage insurance.

The executive order signed Thursday directs the Federal Housing Finance Agency — which oversees mortgage giants Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac — to create a pilot program that would automatically cancel borrowers' mortgage insurance premiums when they have sufficient equity in their homes.

Hundreds of thousands of borrowers use private mortgage insurance each year to qualify for conventional mortgages when they put less than 20% down on their homes. Currently, borrowers can contact their lender and have the insurance canceled when their equity position reaches 20%, and lenders must automatically drop the insurance once the owner has 22% equity, meaning the pilot would streamline existing processes.

PMI premium amounts vary depending on factors like credit score and down payment size, but Freddie Mac estimates them at $30 to $70 a month per $100,000 borrowed. Some mortgage brokers have reported that they're frequently lower, and U.S. Mortgage Insurers, a trade group for the industry, says premiums are down 25% since 2017.

In recent years, as homes have become more expensive, use of PMI has been on the rise. As of 2024, 36% of conventional mortgage borrowers paid PMI, up from 25.4% in 2016, according to Urban Institute data.

The executive order also aims to address affordability by creating a task force on manufactured housing construction innovation, expanding a pilot that waives title insurance for certain refinancings, and directing officials to lower rates on the small number of home loans made directly by the Department of Veterans Affairs and Department of Agriculture.

Claire Boston is a senior reporter for Yahoo Finance covering housing, mortgages, and home insurance.

articles.title: Trump administration cancels some Canada tariffs amid close midterm races
articles.summary: Sen. Susan Collins, who’s in a tough re-election fight, said she secured from the Trump administration tariff exemptions on some agricultural and forestry items.
articles.body: The Trump administration on Friday said it had granted tariff exemptions on some Canadian imports, an implicit acknowledgement that President Donald Trump’s signature trade policy could be hurting Republican candidates running in the Nov. 3 midterm election. The canceled tariffs include 50% duties on some agricultural items. These duties were applied to Canadian products after the country withdrew from trade negotiations with the Trump administration in late August. Polls show Democrats have a solid chance to win majorities in both the House and Senate. Republican Sen. Susan Collins, who’s facing a tough re-election battle in Maine, first announced the news on social media: “I am pleased to have secured additional tariff exemptions products crucial to Maine’s agricultural industries, including blueberry, potato, apple, and seaweed producers.” She said that plastic boxes, crates, packing materials, refrigeration equipment, sealing and labeling machinery, packing equipment, film, foil and seaweed products were some of the other products getting exemptions. A document posted to the White House website confirmed the action, but it said that the administration was also adding tariffs to “certain valves, carpets, waste products” and other items to make up for the duties it was removing. The White House statement said the move aimed to “further refine the scope of the tariffs” applied to Canada. Collins, in her announcement, said that many “farmers and growers rely on specialized equipment, packaging materials, and other products from Canada that are either unavailable from American suppliers or cannot be replaced without incurring significant expense.” Democrat Troy Jackson, who is challenging Collins for her Senate seat, responded by saying: “Trump’s trade wars have made life harder and more expensive for Mainers. Susan Collins enabled this chaos, voted to confirm the people behind it, and now wants credit for bringing a cup of water to put out the fire.” He added on X: “Mainers needed help long before Susan Collins needed saving.” Collins’ announcement did not mention Trump, only top administration officials such as U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick. The White House announcement made no mention of Collins, who has occasionally sparred with Trump. “I will continue working directly with Administration officials to seek additional relief and encourage a broader trade agreement with Canada, our neighbor, ally, and largest trading partner,” Collins said. The Commerce Department and Office of the U.S. Trade Representative did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Other Republicans have broken with Trump’s most well-known economic policy, too. Mike Rogers, who’s in a tight race for a Senate seat in Michigan, told NBC News last week that he would like to see the trade war with Canada “wrapped up.” After U.S. officials made what Prime Minister Mark Carney called “unfair” and “uneconomic” demands, the U.S. hit Canada with two waves of tariffs, the second of which included the 50% duties. Trump has repeatedly said “there’s nothing they have that we need” from Canada. “We have everything,” Trump said in September. On Sept. 28, Trump predicted that Carney would be removing tariffs. “I think what’s going to happen is over the next three or four weeks, they’re going to come to us, and they’re going to say, ‘we’re going to get rid of all the tariffs,’” the president said. “We’re going to win everything,” Trump predicted. “They’re going to come in, and they’re going to say, ‘Sir, we are sorry.’” Asked about Trump’s prediction a day later, Carney laughed during a press conference, adding that he had no additional comment to make. Carney has stood steady in the face of repeated verbal attacks from Trump since the trade war kicked off in August. As Trump has ramped up social media attacks, Carney has turned to the rest of the world, opening up Canada’s economy to China, India, and the United Kingdom. Next week, Carney is set to reach a historic agreement with the European Union over the terms of becoming the bloc’s first-ever “associate member” during an E.U.-Canada summit in Montreal. The European Union’s 27 member states collectively are the world’s single largest trading bloc and the union is the world’s third largest behind the U.S. and China.

articles.title: Treasury moves to ease access to single-family home purchases ahead of midterms
articles.summary: The Treasury Department on Thursday moved to implement tenets of a bipartisan housing law Congress passed over the summer, including a ban on institutional investors buying single-family homes. Under impending regulations from the department, a large institutional investor cannot buy a single-family home starting on Jan. 7, 2027, with certain exceptions. The department is codifying…
articles.body:
The Treasury Department on Thursday moved to implement tenets of a bipartisan housing law Congress passed over the summer , including a ban on institutional investors buying single-family homes.

Under impending regulations from the department, a large institutional investor cannot buy a single-family home starting on Jan. 7, 2027, with certain exceptions.

The department is codifying the ban under the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, a landmark housing law both chambers passed with overwhelming majorities in July.

The likes of progressive Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.) and Rep. French Hill (R-Ark.) championed the legislation , which is intended to reduce federal review processes for housing construction and boost the nation’s supply of units .

President Trump, however, did not sign the measure into law — as he protested Senate Republicans’ inability to pass voter ID legislation , one of his top priorities. The housing law took effect in July, without the president’s signature.

Trump earlier this year signed an executive order directing his administration to crack down on institutional investors purchasing single-family homes.

The new housing law defines a “large” institutional investor as an entity that has direct or indirect investment control over at least 350 homes. It exempts multiple types of purchases from the ban, including those made under build-to-rent programs, renovate-to-rent programs and programs to boost homeownership.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said in a Thursday release the administration “continues to restore the path to affordable homeownership for millions of young and working families.”

Bessent added, “Treasury is working to ensure American families and workers have a fair shot at purchasing homes in their communities by increasing housing supply and limiting large institutional investors’ role in the market, while supporting a strong, stable housing market and avoiding unnecessary disruption.”

The Treasury Department unveiled the regulations less than two weeks before the midterm elections , as Republicans fight to keep control of Congress in the face of Americans’ growing economic frustrations .

However, housing experts say Wall Street investors do not own enough homes to significantly skew housing prices .

“Depending on the threshold used to classify an investor as institutional vs. a mid-sized investor, the total homes owned ranges from approximately 500,000 to 800,000,” Sean Fergus, the vice president of economic research at Zonda, told The Hill in January. “Even assuming the high end of that range, it’s only 0.5 percent of total units and still under 1 percent of the roughly 100 million single-family homes in the country.”

Housing sales have slowed amid high mortgage rates . Pending home sales decreased by 7.3 percent from August to September, according to the National Association of Realtors , and Freddie Mac reported Thursday that the average 30-year fixed mortgage rate this week was 7.32 percent.

Also on Thursday, Trump signed an executive order aimed at lowering government-backed mortgage payments .

articles.title: Collins says certain Canadian goods now tariff-exempt
articles.summary: Sen. Susan Collins (R-Maine) announced Friday that nine categories of Canadian products “crucial for Maine’s agricultural industries” will be exempted from U.S. tariffs. The types of exempted goods include paperboard cartons, plastic boxes, refrigeration equipment, agricultural cleaning and sorting machinery, packing and wrapping machinery and seaweed and algae products, among others, according to a press release…
articles.body:
Sen. Susan Collins (R-Maine) announced Friday that nine categories of Canadian products “crucial for Maine’s agricultural industries” will be exempted from U.S. tariffs.

The types of exempted goods include paperboard cartons, plastic boxes, refrigeration equipment, agricultural cleaning and sorting machinery, packing and wrapping machinery and seaweed and algae products, among others, according to a press release from Collins’s office.

“Many of our farmers and growers rely on specialized equipment, packaging materials, and other products from Canada that are either unavailable from American suppliers or cannot be replaced without incurring significant expense,” the Maine senator said Friday in a post on the social platform X.

She added, “In my repeated conversations with Ambassador Greer, Secretary Lutnick, and other senior Administration officials, I have asked for tariff relief for these important products and I will continue working directly with Administration officials to seek additional relief and encourage a broader trade agreement with Canada, our neighbor, ally, and largest trading partner.”

White House spokesperson Matthew Middleton told The Hill in a statement that the president signed a proclamation Friday “further refining the scope of the tariffs on certain Canadian products previously announced on July 20, 2026 and modified on September 8, 2026.”

“The President is taking action in response to Canada’s continued discrimination against and additional retaliation targeting U.S. commerce, with the goal of protecting American farmers, manufacturers, and workers,” Middleton added.

In late August, Collins criticized President Trump’s decision to impose sweeping 50 percent tariffs on $20 billion worth of Canadian goods after trade negotiations between Washington and Ottawa fell through. Canada’s prime minister, Mark Carney, announced shortly after that his government would match these duties “dollar for dollar.”

The Maine Republican reiterated her concerns when the U.S. threatened additional duties on its northern neighbor, set to go into effect Jan. 1, 2027.

“I still think imposing new tariffs on Canada is a mistake,” Collins said after Trump proposed the New Year’s Day taxes.

In September, the senator announced the exemption of two products — road salt and cement — from the U.S. tariffs on Canada, after she sent a letter to the Trump administration explaining how crucial they are for Maine’s economy.

“I mentioned in a letter to the Administration that Frenchville, a small Maine town on the Canadian border, would incur $10,000 in extra costs for road salt, threatening the town’s ability to provide municipal services. I also shared that I had heard from Maine ready-mix cement company owners, one of whom told me his company would pay $150,000 each month because of this tariff,” Collins said at the time.

Friday’s announcement comes less than two weeks ahead of the midterm elections, where Collins will face off against Democrat Troy Jackson, a former state lawmaker, for a seat in the Senate. The Hill’s election forecasting partner Decision Desk HQ gives Jackson a 55 percent chance of winning the race against the incumbent Republican.

articles.title: Pricey cookie vendor pulls out of some SoCal locations
articles.summary: The popular cookie chain Crumbl has closed nearly 60 locations nationwide, including 7 in California.
articles.body:
Crumbl, the high-end dessert chain serving up oversized cookies , has closed a swath of stores nationwide including seven in California.

Two of the shuttered cookie shops are in Southern California , in Westlake Village and Mira Mesa in San Diego.

The other closed California locations are in Paso Robles, Pismo Beach, Hanford, Ladera Ranch and Cupertino.

Crumbl has reportedly closed 57 locations across the country , including in Florida and Alabama. The chain still has more than 1,000 locations nationwide and more than 100 in California.

The chain was founded by cousins Sawyer Hemsley and Jason McGowan in Utah in 2017 and remains headquartered there. It has exploded in growth since going viral during the pandemic and garnering more than 10 million followers on TikTok.

The cookie shops have a rotating menu of cookies with elaborate toppings, sometimes offering bizarre flavors such as everything bagel. A single cookie from Crumbl costs about $5.

Crumbl has reached customers by embracing third-party delivery and establishing celebrity partnerships with big names, including Kendall Jenner and Olivia Rodrigo.

Though it grew rapidly in the early 2020s, the chain began to face challenges after taking up to $500 million in cash or loans from private equity firms, Bloomberg reported .

In 2022, the company violated child labor laws in six states. Earlier this year, a push to promote "dirty sodas" fell short as the product didn't earn nationwide popularity.

McGowan and Hemsley stepped down as chief executive and chief brand officer, respectively, in May, but they remain on the company's board.

The cousins started the company with no formal baking experience, instead using data-driven testing to develop successful recipes.

Foot traffic has slowed since May, with Restaurant Business reporting that sales in August were 70% lower than they were two years ago.

Crumbl did not immediately respond to a request for comment and has made no indication that it will wind down its business anytime soon.

This story originally appeared in Los Angeles Times .

articles.title: FCC Democrat warns broadcasters to resist Trump’s media pressure tactics
articles.summary: Democrat Anna Gomez warns broadcasters against yielding to the Trump-era FCC’s claims of fake polls and news distortions.
articles.body:
Anna Gomez, the sole Democratic member of the United States Federal Communications Commission (FCC), called on the National Association of Broadcasters (NAB) to ramp up its response to pressure from the administration of US President Donald Trump on major news networks and broadcast television stations in advance of the midterm elections on November 3.

“I would not be doing my job if I did not say plainly that the volume of that response has not yet matched the scale of what your members are facing,” Gomez said in a four-page letter to the industry group’s CEO and President Curtis LeGeyt on Thursday.

Gomez pointed to a recent assertion by Trump-appointed Brenden Carr , who claimed that administration channels could violate their regulatory obligations by airing “entirely fake polls” before the consequential midterm elections, which may determine which political party controls both houses of the US Congress.

“Many journalists and broadcasters have been amplifying or airing these Polls without regard to basic journalistic ethics and without informing the public that those Polls lack a scientific, accurate, or even real basis,” Carr said in a post on the social media platform X.

Al Jazeera reached out to the FCC for clarity on which journalists and broadcasters allegedly aired fake polls and which polls he was referring to, but the agency did not address Al Jazeera’s inquiry.

Seth Stern, the chief of advocacy at the Freedom of the Press Foundation, criticised Carr’s comments.

“Brendan Carr is not the journalism police. And he is just about the least qualified person in the country to lecture the press about journalistic ethics. The tell is that literally every time he attacks the press, it’s because of reporting that was unfavorable to his boss,” Stern said in a statement.

Carr said in his social media post that “Broadcasters are advised to avoid engaging in News Distortions or running Broadcast Hoaxes”.

“This Administration is running a coordinated, government-wide effort to reshape the media into its sanctioned messenger, and the Federal Communications Commission has become one of its most active instruments. That is playing out across several fronts. One of the most brazen efforts involves how this Commission has recently suggested that broadcasters who air polling that does not align with this Administration’s preferred narrative could face an FCC news distortion or broadcast hoax investigation,” Gomez said in her letter.

Gomez added that there is a high barrier for proof of news distortion for it to be actionable, saying that it only applies when a broadcaster “knowingly airs false information about a crime or catastrophe and that broadcast directly causes immediate and substantial harm to public safety or property”.

Gomez added that the agency does not have the authority to act unless there is clear evidence.

“Reporting the results of a poll this Administration happens to dislike does not come close to meeting those standards,” Gomez said.

articles.body: MUMBAI: The maiden public offering for Jio Platforms, which aimed to raise a recordbreaking Rs 30,213 crore, on Friday created several other records. It saw about 1.3 crore retail investors participating in the offer. While the institutional part was subscribed more than 70 times, the total demand for shares, including the anchor part in the offer, touched almost Rs 7.5 lakh crore.The earlier record for applications in an IPO was for Waaree Energies in which a little over 97 lakh investors had applied. In 2008, the Reliance Power IPO had seen the total demand at about Rs 7.1 lakh crore. At Friday’s close of bidding, Jio IPO surpassed both these marks.On Day 1, India’s biggest IPO was fully subscribed within the first 100 minutes of opening, exchange data had shown. At close, the institutional (QIB) part of the IPO, in which a little over 4.9 crore shares were offered, was subscribed 70.6 times, while the HNI portion, in which about 3.6 crore shares were reserved, was subscribed 14 times.Exchange data also showed that the portion reserved for Jio employees was subscribed nearly three times while the part reserved for RIL shareholders was subscribed 7.6 times. The portion marked for retail investors, in which about 8.5 crore shares were offered, was subscribed 2.7 times.In the unofficial market, speculators are betting that the company will be listing at about Rs 1,370, a mark-up (also called the grey market premium or GMP) of about Rs 250 over the upper limit of the IPO price band of Rs 1,065 to Rs 1,119. articles.title: Hedge Funds Are Record Short Natural Gas on Mild Winter Outlook
articles.summary: Hedge-fund managers have amassed a record short position in US natural gas on expectations for an unusually mild northern winter that points to anemic demand...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Hedge-fund managers have amassed a record short position in US natural gas on expectations for an unusually mild northern winter that points to anemic demand for the furnace and power-plant fuel.

Money managers have increased short-only exposure, or bets on prices falling, across seven benchmark Henry Hub contracts to 599,731, according to Commodity Futures Trading Commission data released Friday. It's the largest in data going back to May 2013.

The net-short position on US gas rose to 192,728, the most bearish in more than six years, while bullish bets dropped to the lowest in almost two years.

Benchmark US gas futures plummeted more than 15% for the largest weekly decline since February, as forecasts shifted warmer for the first months of the northern winter. Gas bulls typically count on colder weather to boost demand for the fuel to run furnaces and power plants.

Commodity Weather Group is predicting this month and next will be the third-warmest months in records going back to 1950.

The bearish bets, while reflecting traders' growing conviction that the so-called Super El Niño weather pattern will bring very mild weather, also increases the risk of a short squeeze. Any sudden, severe cold snap can send gas demand surging while slashing production, lifting prices as traders scramble to rapidly close out short positions to forestall losses.

A winter storm-driven short squeeze exacerbated the historic gas rally that took place in late January, when money managers reduced short-only positions by more than 53,000 lots in a single week, the largest decline in more than a year.

articles.summary: MUMBAI: RBI’s net dollar purchases surged 132% to $43.3 billion in Aug 2026, driven by inflows through its concessional FCNR(B) swap facility, while its
articles.body: MUMBAI: RBI’s net dollar purchases surged 132% to $43.3 billion in Aug 2026, driven by inflows through its concessional FCNR(B) swap facility, while its outstanding net forward short position crossed $200 billion for the first time.RBI bought $74.5 billion in dollars during the month, up 93.9% from $38.4 billion in July. It made no dollar purchases in Aug 2025, when it was defending the rupee amid foreign portfolio outflows. Dollar sales rose 57.9% month-on-month to $31.2 billion from $19.8 billion in July and were 305.6% higher than the $7.7 billion sold in Aug 2025.Net purchases were 132% higher than the $18.7 billion recorded in July and contrasted with net sales of $7.7 billion in Aug 2025. Gross transactions across onshore and offshore over-the-counter markets exceeded $105.7 billion. RBI’s dollar purchases helped absorb the $127 billion mobilised by banks through FCNR(B) deposits from NRIs.However, pressure on the rupee prompted the central bank to sell dollars to support the currency. Its dollar sales of $31.2 billion in Aug represented around a quarter of the amount mobilised through FCNR(B) deposits, though the two figures cover different types of transactions and periods of currency management.India’s foreign exchange reserves fell by $5.01 billion to $721.02 billion in the week ended Oct 16, down $64.7 billion from their all-time high of $785.71 billion in the week ended Sept 4, as pressure on the rupee continued. Foreign currency assets, the largest component of reserves, declined by $5.76 billion during the latest week. The fall was partly offset by a $706 million increase in the value of gold reserves.RBI’s concessional dollar-rupee swap facility allowed banks to exchange dollar deposits raised from NRIs for three to five years for rupees, while securing forward hedges from the central bank. The deposit mobilisation window closed at the end of Aug, prompting banks to surrender the dollar proceeds to RBI.The central bank also stepped up dollar sales and conducted offsetting sellbuy swaps to manage the rupee and the liquidity injected through its purchases. Its outstanding net forward short position rose by $63.3 billion, or 46.3%, in a month to a record $200.1 billion at end-Aug, compared with $136.8 billion in July and $53.4 billion a year earlier.You use AI every day. articles.body: MUMBAI: Outward remittances under RBI’s Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS) rose 6% month-on-month to $2.7 billion in Aug 2026, driven by overseas student travel, business travel and payments for remote education, while investments in foreign equity and debt more than doubled from a year earlier.Travel accounted for 59.5% of total remittances, rising 11.4% from July to $1.6 billion. articles.body: BENGALURU: Infosys had a lacklustre Q2, with its shares falling 6% in early trade on the NYSE after it cut FY27 revenue growth guidance to 1%-2% in constant currency terms from 1.5%-3% earlier. This is the company’s weakest growth outlook in seven years, reflecting subdued volumes, pricing pressure and weakness in its mainstay market, North America, which declined 1.5% year on year.The slowdown was particularly sharp in high-tech and retail, which declined 17.3% and 7.7% year on year, respectively, in constant currency terms.Infosys CEO Salil Parekh said the weakness was driven by specific client situations rather than a broad-based slowdown across industries. “We have seen different client-specific situations in both retail and high-tech. We continue to see strong growth and discretionary spending in financial services, energy and utilities, and manufacturing,” he said.CFO Jayesh Sanghrajka said volumes remained subdued, while competitive intensity and clients’ higher productivity expectations had put pressure on pricing. Discretionary spending in retail and high-tech was also lower than anticipated, he said, adding that these factors had led to the guidance cut.Retail was additionally affected by a larger thirdparty component in the previous quarters, creating an unfavourable sequential comparison. articles.title: Two critical PHP flaws trigger global alert; millions of services face cyber risk
articles.summary: BENGALURU: Two critical PHP vulnerabilities that could allow hackers to remotely execute code on servers without authentication have triggered a
articles.body: BENGALURU: Two critical PHP vulnerabilities that could allow hackers to remotely execute code on servers without authentication have triggered a cybersecurity alert, potentially exposing millions of internet-facing services. In a separate advisory, PHP also urged users to temporarily disable a file-upload tracking feature to mitigate another remote code execution risk, adding to concerns over the widely used programming language.PHP advised users on Oct 23 to temporarily disable its session upload progress feature until the next regular bugfix release. The warning followed an earlier advisory on Oct 21 about a related vulnerability. The latest issue affects applications only when specific session settings are changed while running and the upload progress feature remains enabled. Users who have already disabled the feature do not need to take further action.The broader concerns centre on two critical vulnerabilities collectively referred to as PHP2Shell. Aamir Lakhani, global director of threat intelligence and adversarial artificial intelligence research at Fortinet, said: “Two critical PHP vulnerabilities disclosed this week pose an urgent security and business continuity risk for organizations that depend on websites, customer portals, and other web applications.”PHP is a server-side programming language used by widely deployed platforms such as WordPress, Drupal, Joomla and Magento. Companies can be exposed through commercial applications, hosting providers and embedded software components even if they do not develop PHP applications themselves.The potential scale of exposure is significant. Censys identified approximately 36.7 million internet-facing services reporting potentially affected PHP versions in its Oct 22 snapshot. These are service counts, not unique servers or organisations, and may include installations already patched through vendor updates.Saeed Abbasi, head of the Threat Research Unit and director of product at Qualys, said the company found 167 million PHP package installations across 12,000 organisations, with 73% deployed on internet-facing assets, putting them within reach of remote attackers. “Applying a patch alone will not be sufficient for systems running unsupported versions, where upgrading is the only viable long-term solution. The key takeaway is that nearly all PHP installations are either vulnerable or running unsupported versions,” he said.CloudSEK said Shodan identified 2.2 million internet-facing services displaying PHP information worldwide, with India ranking ninth at 53,400 services. Of 36,700 Indian services revealing their PHP versions, about 36,100 were unpatched, including 19,500 running versions that have reached end of life, said Akash Karthi, a security researcher at CloudSEK.You use AI every day. articles.title: Upper layer NBFCs have to list: RBI governor on Tatas; dispels doubts on Sept order
articles.summary: Mumbai: In his first public comment since Reserve Bank of India rejected Tata Sons’ bid to shed its non-bank lender status, governor Sanjay Malhotra on
articles.body: Mumbai: In his first public comment since Reserve Bank of India rejected Tata Sons’ bid to shed its non-bank lender status, governor Sanjay Malhotra on Friday left little doubt that the Tata Group holding company must list publicly as long as it remains classified as an upper-layer (UL) non-banking financial company (NBFC) and core investment company (CIC).The remarks appear to settle a debate sparked by Noel Tata, chair of Tata Trusts, Tata Sons’ largest shareholder, who had argued that RBI’s Sept 11 order, which rejected the holding company’s request to deregister as a CIC and directed it to comply with UL-NBFC regulations, did not explicitly mandate a listing.Malhotra’s comments also suggest Tata Sons is in breach of RBI rules. The consequences of continued noncompliance remain unclear.The governor declined to be drawn into the question of Noel Tata’s proposal to merge two Tata Sons subsidiaries with the holding company, a move that could help it sidestep a stock market listing.“NBFCs and CICs, like for example Tata Sons and others, are required to be registered with us because of the systemic risks,” Malhotra said.“As long as it is an NBFC within our definition, it’s a CIC and has access to funds direct or indirect, it’s required to be registered and if it is in the upper layer, it is required to list,” he said at NDTV’s World Summit conference Friday.RBI first classified Tata Sons as an UL-NBFC in 2022 and required it to list within three years. The holding company sought to avoid a market debut by applying to surrender its CIC registration after reducing its debt to zero. But in Sept, the central bank rejected the request, saying it “cannot be acceded to”.‘CICs sit atop group cos, can leverage funds through them’RBI requires UL-NBFCs with assets exceeding Rs 1 lakh crore, or direct or indirect access to public funds, to list. With assets of Rs 2.01 lakh crore as of March 31, 2026, Tata Sons comfortably exceeds the threshold. Malhotra said CICs sit atop group companies and can leverage funds through them, exposing money raised from banks, corporate bonds and other sources to risk.Days after receiving the RBI letter, the Tata Sons board discussed the regulator’s decision at its Sept 17 meeting and agreed to comply with RBI regulations, but did not take a call on listing.Noel Tata, who is also a director of Tata Sons, has asked the company to explore alternatives to a market debut. He told the board: “It (the RBI’s communique) does not mention listing. It prescribes no particular step, and it does not say that the company is in breach.” He added that the board had formed no view on the legal effect of the RBI’s communication or what actions it required Tata Sons to take and by when.You use AI every day. articles.title: Trump ends tariffs on some Canadian products, aiming to help Senator Collins
articles.summary: WASHINGTON, Oct 23 (Reuters) - With an incumbent Maine US senator from his own party locked in a tight reelection battle, President Donald Trump signed an or...
articles.body:
WASHINGTON, Oct 23 (Reuters) - With an incumbent Maine US senator from his own party locked in a tight reelection battle, President Donald Trump signed an order on Friday to remove 50% tariffs on some Canadian agricultural and forestry products in a move that could ‌benefit companies from the state.

The Republican president's hefty tariffs on Canada have caused friction with the US neighbor to the north while creating problems for ‌American businesses in Maine and other states that rely on certain Canadian goods.

With the November 3 US midterm elections looming and Republicans fighting to retain control of Congress, Senator Susan Collins had urged the ​White House to address tariffs on products affecting Maine companies and farmers.

Trump's order exempted plywood sheets, some paper products, certain machinery and refrigeration equipment, and packing crates and boxes, as well as fresh and dried seaweed, the White House said.

The changes take effect on October 30, four days before the election.

Trump added a number of Canadian products to the 50% tariff list to offset the tariff relief provided in his order, including carpets, paints, shampoos, cocoa powder, wooden coffins, ice cream sticks, air-conditioning machines, chest freezers, archery equipment ‌and canoes.

Collins said the relief will aid Maine's blueberry, potato, ⁠apple and seaweed producers.

"These producers are a vital part of our state's economy and support our rural and coastal communities," Collins said. "Many of our farmers and growers rely on specialized equipment, packaging materials and other products from Canada that are either unavailable from ⁠American suppliers or cannot be replaced without incurring significant expense."

Democrat Troy Jackson is seeking to oust Collins in next month's election in a race that polls indicate is very close. The two sparred over tariffs at an October 6 debate.

"Trump's trade wars have made life harder and more expensive for Mainers," Jackson said on Friday after Trump's action. "Susan Collins enabled this ​chaos, ​voted to confirm the people behind it, and now wants credit for bringing a cup of ​water to put out the fire."

Trump in August imposed 50% tariffs ‌on $20 billion of Canadian imports, which took effect after talks between the two countries collapsed. Canada retaliated in September with tariffs ranging from 15% to 50% on $20 billion in US goods.

Canada and the United States have been engaged in a standoff over the tariffs since Trump imposed them. Trump on Friday asserted that Canada is working on a deal.

Stocks slide as oil prices rise again ahead of midterms

Stocks tumbled on Friday , as oil prices rose again amid the ongoing U.S.-Iran and Russia-Ukraine conflicts.

At closing, the Nasdaq Composite was down roughly 53.5 points from Thursday. The index is down by more than 1,600 points since closing time on Oct. 6, when it finished at its highest mark of the year.

The S&P 500, meanwhile, sunk by nearly 40 points since Thursday’s closing. The index dipped as low as 7,612, its lowest point in more than a month.

Brent crude, the international benchmark, is trading at almost $116 per barrel as of Friday, its highest point since late April — roughly two months into the Iran war.

West Texas Intermediate crude, the standard for North American markets, closed at $103.44 , after reaching $103.92 earlier in the day.

The rise in oil prices from geopolitical shocks has carried harsh consequences for Americans, who are paying higher prices at the pump ahead of the midterm elections.

Regular gas costs roughly $4.29 per gallon on average, while the price of a gallon of diesel is above $6.30, according to data from AAA.

That lends President Trump and the GOP a tough hand with voting already underway, as Democrats seek to take control of Congress for the bulk of the president’s final two years in office.

“Gas and diesel prices will continue to skyrocket based on the policies of [Trump] and his Republican enablers,” Rep. Ted Lieu (D-Calif), the No. 4 House Democrat, wrote Friday on social platform X. “November is coming.”

articles.title: Trump eases tariffs on Canadian imports weeks before US midterms, offering relief to Maine
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump’s administration has eased some tariffs on Canadian imports, with the move coming just two weeks before the November 3 midterm
articles.body: US President Donald Trump’s administration has eased some tariffs on Canadian imports, with the move coming just two weeks before the November 3 midterm elections. The decision could benefit Republican Senator Susan Collins, who is facing a tough re-election contest in Maine, a state whose economy has been affected by the trade dispute with Canada.The White House said the changes would remove tariffs on certain products, including "plywood sheets, some paper products, certain machinery and refrigeration equipment". However, the administration will also introduce tariffs on other goods, including carpets, certain valves and waste products. The new measures will take effect on October 30.Collins said she had "secured" the exemptions for products important to Maine's agricultural sector, including blueberry, potato, apple and seaweed producers.Collins seeks relief for Maine businessesCollins, who faces a strong challenge from a Democratic candidate, said farmers in her state depend on supplies from Canada that are difficult or expensive to source elsewhere.She said many farmers "rely on specialized equipment, packaging materials, and other products from Canada that are either unavailable from American suppliers or cannot be replaced without incurring significant expense."The senator's intervention comes as Democrats target her seat in their bid to take control of Congress from Republicans in the November 3 midterm elections. Maine shares a border with Canada, and businesses in the state have felt the effects of Trump's trade policies.The partial tariff relief could ease costs for some businesses, although the introduction of duties on other Canadian products means the changes will not benefit every sector.Trade tensions strain US-Canada tiesThe United States and Canada have closely connected economies, with roughly 70 per cent of Canadian exports going to the US. Trade relations have deteriorated since negotiations between the two countries broke down in August, prompting Trump to impose a fresh round of tariffs.Earlier US duties on Canadian cars, steel, aluminium and lumber have hurt businesses, contributed to job losses and weighed on economic growth. Canada entered a technical recession this year after its economy contracted for two consecutive quarters.The tariffs imposed after the collapse of trade talks affected goods worth around $20 billion, equivalent to 5.5 per cent of Canadian exports to the US. The targeted products ranged from hockey sticks to cement.Since returning to office for his second term, Trump has imposed extensive tariffs on imports from both allies and rivals, arguing that other countries have taken advantage of the United States.His administration has also linked some threatened tariffs to broader political and foreign policy goals.You use AI every day.
